title: IAS 16 Layer-2 teaching-body audit — elaboration sufficiency and duplication
base_subject: Densify five IAS 16 medium teaching gaps (#86)
verdict_plain: The teaching spine is dense enough to study, and most Illustrations carry a distinct test or unique numbers. Dedupe is required for nine units that repeat the same point, including one Critical pair (EY Illustration 3-3 pumps in Ch2 and Ch6). Densify is required for a small set of named DTT initial-cost plates that are still absent or one line.

chapter_one_liners.one_liner: Glossary table only; chapters do not re-teach the defined terms.
Scope, exclusions, bearer and boundary Illustrations are distinct; paragraph 5 is taught in both 1.2 and 1.4.
Recognition spine is dense; safety Illustrations 2.4.1 and 2.4.2 are the same test, and the pump plate is repeated in Chapter 6.
Cost build, 20A and exchanges are sufficient; customer-contribution and contingent Illustrations restate their sections, and four DTT cost plates are still absent.
Class, mechanics and surplus Illustrations use distinct numbers; Illustration 4.0.1 restates the new policy heading with no journal.
Component, residual, method and estimate plates keep unique numbers; units-of-production stays prose because the KPMG method tables are blank.
Undivided-interest fraction, rental fleet, insurance and IFRS 5 are distinct; the pump plate and the physical-part Illustration repeat earlier prose.
Reconciliation mapping and 74A(a) use an extra test; commitments and 74A(b) Illustrations restate the section and carry no amounts.

top_10.issue: Same EY Illustration 3-3 pump plate (CU10 million, CU200,000, CU170,000, CU51,000) written twice. Chapter 6 adds only that the CU51,000 write-off is a paragraph 68/71 loss.
Customer-contribution Illustration repeats control, fair value, stand-alone selling price, and the tooling / utility / outsourcing examples already in the section. No currency plate.
Contingent-consideration Illustration repeats the two observed approaches already set out side by side. No currency plate. Illustration 3.7A.2 is a later test and can stay.
Policy-change Illustration repeats cost-to-revaluation versus revaluation-to-cost with no worked journal.
Commitments Illustration repeats paragraph 74(a)–(c) and the DTT cumulative-CIP reading already in the section, and states that the sources give no amounts.
74A(b) Illustration repeats the disclosure limb and points at Illustration 3.5.1, with no proceeds or cost figure. Illustration 7.5.1 stays: it splits Company W’s 800 from the 200.
Physical-part Illustration repeats the section’s allocation rule and states that no currency amount is given. Illustration 6.0A.1 stays: 25% leaves and 75% remains.
Paragraph 5 cost-model investment property, fair-value investment property staying in IAS 40, and investment property under construction are taught in both sections.
Chemical-handling and emissions-filter plates are the same paragraph 11 capitalise-and-review-combined-carrying-amount test. KPMG Example 16 adds no distinct view and no numbers.

DTT A7 4.2.6 reimbursement, 4.2.7 broker rebate, 4.2.8 utility capacity fee and 4.2.9-2 occupation approval are absent. New obligations after acquisition (DTT 4.2.10-1, KPMG Example 7) are one sentence.

critical: Keep one pump plate. Put the paragraph 68/71 loss sentence on the home plate (Illustration 2.6.2) and replace Illustration 6.5.1 with a one-line pointer that keeps id s-6-ex-replace-pump.
medium: Collapse agreeing #55 Illustrations that have no unique numbers into the section already written: 3.1A.1, 3.7A.1, 4.0.1, 6.0A.2, 7.4.1, 7.5.2. Keep chips on the surviving unit.
Make §1.4 the only home of paragraph 5; reduce §1.2 to a one-line pointer.
Fold KPMG Example 16 into Illustration 2.4.1 as a second fact chip, or drop Illustration 2.4.2.
Densify from extractable DTT text only: reimbursement, broker rebate, utility capacity fee, occupation approval, and the asbestos / new-obligation example. No invented currency.
nice: Shorten §4.10 to a one-line pointer to Chapter 6.
Units-of-production numeric plate only if a non-blank firm table is attached (KPMG Examples 12A–12C are blank).
IFRIC 1 revaluation-model journals only if KPMG Examples 6B–6D tables are no longer blank.
Optional later tips: EY 4.2.2 liquidated damages, EY 3.1.3 pre-permission, PwC FAQ 22.22.5, PwC FAQ 22.71.2, EY section 6.5 ROU revaluation.
Strip author-meta sentences from new Illustrations (sources state no amount; this plate is not an extract).

out_of_scope_respected: IAS 38 and IAS 40 packs not opened
proposed_workbook_56_remarks: Layer-2 body audit on main da18653 (post #86). Verdict BOTH. Critical DUP: EY Illustration 3-3 pumps live as Illustration 2.6.2 and Illustration 6.5.1 with the same CU. Medium DUP: six #55-era Illustrations restate their own section with no unique numbers (3.1A.1, 3.7A.1, 4.0.1, 6.0A.2, 7.4.1, 7.5.2), paragraph 5 is in both 1.2 and 1.4, and safety Illustrations 2.4.1 and 2.4.2 are one test. Medium THIN: DTT 4.2.6–4.2.9-2 absent; asbestos / new-obligation is one sentence. 145 of 154 walked units are OK, including the distinct-number plates in Chapters 4 and 5 and the extra-test disclosure plates 7.3.1 and 7.5.1. Do not invent FS images or blank KPMG journals. HTML not edited in this workbook.
